solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: More heat, love, quickly!

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective or adverb of musical pace; 'quickly' is the adverb

parts.note: when prices go up there is more
short for temperature, a measure of heat
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An impatient lover urges a partner to turn up the heat and hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'heat' makes the clue sound like a lover's command, but 'quickly' is the whole definition, in the musical sense of pace.
explanation.definitionFit: Music played at a faster pace is described this way, so it moves along rapidly, at speed.

clue.text: Superior flat mobile phone — use with temperature reduced internally

indicators.note: something placed internally goes inside another group of letters
something mobile moves about, so these letters are free to be moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
temperature cut down to its abbreviation

explanation.surface: Advice on using a mobile phone at a lowered temperature in a posh flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mobile phone' looks like one fixed phrase, but 'mobile' is the anagram signal, and it works on the words after the dash too.
explanation.definitionFit: A penthouse is the luxurious top-floor apartment of a building, above and grander than the rest.

clue.text: Ogle organ in a state of arousal

parts.note: the eye is an organ of sight
up as in awake and roused

explanation.surface: A leering double entendre about a certain organ getting excited.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface steers the mind to a less polite organ; the organ is the one used for looking, and being up means being roused from sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: To eye someone up is to look them over with obvious desire, which is leering or ogling.

clue.text: One enrolled in scheme to get gas — antidote to politician's speech?

indicators.note: someone enrolled in a group is taken inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a scheme is a plan
the Roman numeral for one
to gas is to chatter idly

explanation.surface: A member of a scheme gets gas supplied, set against a politician's windy speeches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gas' pretends to be fuel from a scheme, but in the sense of empty chatter it gives TALK; the question mark flags the playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Politicians are mocked for evasive waffle, so honest, direct and straightforward speech is the cure for it.

clue.text: Labour's curse: "Nothing right!"

parts.note: 'eff' is a euphemistic swear word, as in 'eff off'
zero, shaped like O
RT is an abbreviation of right

explanation.surface: A complaint about the Labour Party: nothing it does goes right.
explanation.walkthrough: Labour looks like the political party but is ordinary hard work; 'eff' is a mild stand-in for a four-letter swear word.
explanation.definitionFit: Labour in its sense of hard work or exertion is a close synonym, both meaning energetic toil.

clue.text: (& 11ac.) Easy-going supporter: "City's losing it for nothing"

parts.note: a fan supports a team

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so letters drop out

parts.note: taken as written, before trimming
taken as written; these letters are removed
something given for nothing costs nothing

explanation.surface: A relaxed football fan grumbles that City are losing for no reason.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City's losing it' sounds like the team losing their composure, but IT is literally taken out of CITY, leaving CY.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fancy-free has no romantic ties or worries and so is relaxed, carefree and unconcerned.

clue.text: If film's almost too dirty, you're not allowed in

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
something dirty is messed up, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the apostrophe ignored
the word with its last letter cut

explanation.surface: An X-rated film: if it is too dirty, you will not be admitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too dirty' reads as a phrase about the film, but 'almost' trims 'too' and 'dirty' then scrambles it with IF and FILMS.
explanation.definitionFit: A place that is off limits is out of bounds, so entry there is forbidden to you.

clue.text: Effective power of the heartless and the reckless

indicators.note: something reckless is wild and uncontrolled, so these letters are thrown into disorder
without a heart means the central letter is taken away

parts.note: the word with its middle letter removed
the same word with its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A sour observation that real power belongs to the cruel and the rash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The heartless and the reckless' reads as two kinds of people, but each 'the' is a word to be worked on in turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A law or body with teeth has real force to enforce its will, so the word means genuine clout.

clue.text: Used by tosser to get rid of evidence of time problem?

definitions.text: Used by tosser to get rid of evidence

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
an issue is a problem

explanation.surface: A crude joke about how a certain kind of man tidies up afterwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The long definition is a smutty cryptic description; 'tosser' is British slang for a contemptible man, literally one who masturbates.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper handkerchief is what someone might use for wiping up and disposing of any mess.

clue.text: An Etonian's excited about vote — "It's not going as Putin wants"

definitions.text: It's not going as Putin wants
definitions.note: a cryptic description of the answer as a campaign that is going badly

indicators.note: about means around, so one set of letters surrounds another
an excited thing is agitated and stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of the two words, the 's ignored
a voter marks the ballot paper with a cross

explanation.surface: A posh schoolboy gets worked up over a vote on Russia's war going badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Eton is Britain's most famous public school, so an Etonian is a posh former pupil; 'excited' scrambles those letters around the ballot cross.
explanation.definitionFit: Russia's attempted seizure and incorporation of Ukrainian territory is what has been stalling for Putin.

clue.text: see 6dn.
Nick elected — make a contribution

parts.note: a nick in a cup is a chip
a party that is elected is in power

explanation.surface: A man called Nick wins his seat and is expected to do his bit.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a politician's name, but it is a small notch or chip.
explanation.definitionFit: To chip in is to add one's share, whether of money or of remarks, to a common pot.

clue.text: Broadcaster with pale, see-through top

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite television company
a pale colour is a light one

explanation.surface: A TV presenter wearing a pale, transparent blouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See-through top' suggests clothing, but it is a window set into a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazed window in a roof lets daylight in through the uppermost part of a building.

clue.text: Before match, faces a thankless task

indicators.note: one thing coming before another fixes the order in which the pieces are joined

parts.note: mug is slang for a face
a match is a game

explanation.surface: Before a big match, a team faces a hopeless job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faces' looks like a verb (confronts); here it is a plural noun, slang for faces. A mug is also a gullible fool, hence the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A mug's game is an activity only a fool would take on, since it brings no reward or gratitude.

clue.text: Trail round shopping area — not conducive to sparkling conversation

indicators.note: to go round something is to surround it, so one piece encloses another

parts.note: to trail someone is to stalk them
a mall is a shopping centre

explanation.surface: Trudging round a shopping centre is no place for witty chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trail round' reads like a weary shopping trip, but the trail is a verb for following someone, which wraps round the mall.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite chit-chat about trivial matters like weather is the opposite of lively, brilliant discussion.

clue.text: Heavens! Cyclops is having pee inside — most revealing

definitions.note: a superlative for an adjective in its plain form; very skimpy clothing reveals the most

indicators.note: something put inside goes within another group of letters, held there

parts.note: the heavens are the sky
the setter speaking of himself: I am, contracted
the letter P is pronounced pee

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to relieving himself indoors, exposing rather too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavens!' looks like an exclamation of shock; it is the sky, holding the setter's I'M and the letter P.
explanation.definitionFit: Skimpy clothing covers very little of the body and so shows off a great deal of skin.

clue.text: Evict US Democrat unceremoniously before start of election? Tempting!

indicators.note: coming before fixes which piece goes first in the join
done without ceremony means roughly and in disorder, so the letters are thrown about

parts.note: EVICT and US taken as written, with D for Democrat

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A tempting idea: throwing a US Democrat out on their ear ahead of polling day.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a political wish; 'unceremoniously' is the signal to scramble EVICT, US and D, and 'Tempting!' is both exclamation and definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tempting is alluring and enticing, attractive in a way that draws you towards it.

clue.text: TV host now about to get erection?

parts.note: the present is now

indicators.note: an erection is something raised upright, and in a down entry raising letters turns them upside down

parts.note: re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A smutty question about a TV host who is suddenly aroused on air.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, something that stands erect lifts its letters upward, so they read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who fronts a television programme and introduces its items is called its host.

clue.text: About to ruin king's pronouncement

parts.note: re means about or concerning
to mar is to spoil
K for king in chess notation

explanation.surface: A monarch is on the point of spoiling things with a royal declaration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'on the point of', but 'about' stands alone for RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pronouncement is something said or stated, as is a comment or observation.

clue.text: Dodge party's blue-eyed boy making a comeback

parts.note: a side is a party in a dispute, plus the S

indicators.note: coming back means going the way it came, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: a blue-eyed boy is a favourite, a pet

explanation.surface: A party favourite staging a political comeback while ducking questions.
explanation.walkthrough: A blue-eyed boy is a British idiom for someone's favourite; the 's of 'party's' is kept as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge a question or blow is to step aside and avoid it, which is what the verb means.

clue.text: Cyclops' temperature doubled when held by Sibyl?

indicators.note: something held by another is gripped inside it

parts.note: a sibyl is a prophetess, a seer
T for temperature, twice

explanation.surface: The setter's fever spikes while an oracle takes his temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: Cyclops is the pseudonym of this puzzle's compiler, so the definition is his job title; the apostrophe links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cyclops is the pen name of the person who composes and compiles this crossword puzzle.

clue.text: "Last mismanaged conflict": Putin at heart is resolute

indicators.note: something mismanaged is handled badly and ends up in a muddle, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
a war is a conflict

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter

parts.note: the central letter of the five

explanation.surface: Putin, deep down, is determined, despite his war being badly run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last mismanaged conflict' reads as a headline about a war; 'mismanaged' works only on LAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A stalwart person is loyal, steadfast and unwavering, which is a close synonym for determined.

clue.text: Name-dropping Putin left out — might be found in bed

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the noun

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters are rearranged
dropping something lets it fall away, so that letter is removed

parts.note: N for name; this letter is removed
taken as written, before trimming
L for left

explanation.surface: A name-dropper who omits Putin might end up in bed with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name-dropping' looks like the social habit, but it tells you to drop N from PUTIN; 'bed' is a flower bed, not a bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulips are spring flowers that gardeners plant in rows in flower beds.

clue.text: It trembles like a vice-president avoiding Capitol event leaders

parts.note: as means like

indicators.note: avoiding something means keeping away from it, so those letters are left out

parts.note: Mike Pence was Trump's vice-president

indicators.note: leaders go in front, so the first letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A trembling vice-president keeps away from the Capitol riot and its ringleaders.
explanation.walkthrough: The Capitol event recalls the 2021 riot Pence was caught up in; its leaders are letters to strike out of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar whose leaves quiver in the slightest breeze, hence the trembling aspen.

clue.text: Crummy, crap energy handout ultimately results in reprimand

indicators.note: something crummy is shoddy and badly made, so the letters are knocked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the final letter is taken

parts.note: the closing letter

explanation.surface: A lousy energy subsidy scheme gets its designers a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crummy, crap' reads as a pair of insults, but the first scrambles the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British informal for summoning them to be scolded, originally onto the boss's carpet.

clue.text: Meeting different sorts of people

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a horse-racing meeting, a day at the track
second meaning: ethnic groups of humankind

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as one phrase about mixing socially; a race meeting in British usage is a day of horse races.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun covers both an event at a racecourse and groupings of humanity by ancestry.

clue.text: Part of one's member wrapped in awful nappy

indicators.note: something wrapped in a covering sits inside it, so the letters lie within the words

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A baby's private parts swaddled in a dreadful nappy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' invites a smutty reading, but here it is a limb; a nappy is British for a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The ulna is one of the two long bones of the forearm, so part of an arm, a bodily limb.

clue.text: Vulgar type forced cities' referendum

parts.note: a pleb is a common, vulgar person

indicators.note: something forced is pushed out of its natural shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boorish type imposes a popular vote on the cities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forced' looks like a verb with the pleb as subject, but it scrambles CITIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a direct public vote in which the whole electorate decides a single question.

clue.text: Solemn and humourless, our Brian, having sex

parts.note: po as in po-faced, stern and humourless
Private Eye has long called Charles 'Brian', and he is now king

explanation.surface: A stuffy, joyless character called Brian gets up to something rude.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye's running joke calls the royals Brenda and Brian, so 'our Brian' is the magazine's name for King Charles.
explanation.definitionFit: Poke is vulgar slang for having intercourse, so the gerund stands for the act itself.

clue.text: Determine the size of Bill?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to find the dimensions of something
second meaning: a proposed law put before parliament

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark hints at a man named Bill, but a bill is a legislative proposal.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for sizing up length or quantity and a noun for a piece of legislation.
